description: Spends monthly amounts for a year across every card earnrate knows, and ranks single cards and two-card pairs by rewards minus annual fees, and minus a membership a card needs (a Costco membership) unless the user has it or spends at Costco. Spending is optional: without it, typical U.S. household amounts are used and the answer says so. With `cards` (named in the conversation) or compareToWallet (the saved wallet), it ranks the cards that would add the most to those cards instead. Use it for "which card fits my spending?" or "is it worth adding a card?". It leaves out welcome bonuses.

business.description: Business cards instead of personal ones.

cards.description: Cards the user named in this conversation, to answer for just those cards without saving anything. Leave out to use the user's saved wallet if they have one; with neither, the answer covers every card earnrate knows.

activated.description: Bonuses the user has activated with the issuer, as rule ids from search_cards.

picks.description: Bonus categories the user picked, for cards that have them: choice id → option ids, from search_cards. Ask; don't guess.

compareToWallet.description: Rank the cards that would add the most to the user's saved wallet.

kind.description: cash: cash back cards only. points: points and miles cards only.

memberships.description: Memberships the user has, such as amazon-prime or costco. Rates that need one they don't have are listed separately; a card that needs one (Costco Anywhere) says so.

noAnnualFee.description: Only cards with no annual fee.

spending.description: Monthly spending lines, each a category (grocery.supermarket, dining, gas, other) or a merchant (Amazon, Costco). Optional: leave out to use typical amounts, and don't press the user for numbers they haven't offered.

category.description: A spending category: dining (Restaurants), dining.fast_food (Fast food), grocery.supermarket (Supermarkets), grocery.online (Online grocery and delivery), superstore (Superstores), warehouse_club (Warehouse clubs), convenience_store (Convenience stores), gas (Gas stations), gas.grocery_store (Gas at grocery stores), gas.superstore (Gas at superstores and warehouse clubs), ev_charging (EV charging), transit (Transit), transit.rideshare (Rideshare and taxis), travel (Travel), travel.flights (Flights), travel.hotels (Hotels), travel.car_rental (Car rental), travel.cruise (Cruises), streaming (Streaming services), tv_internet (TV and internet service), phone (Cell phone service), utilities (Home utilities), drugstore (Drugstores and pharmacies), movie_theaters (Movie theaters), entertainment (Live entertainment and events), fitness (Gyms and fitness), department_store (Department stores), clothing (Clothing stores), electronics (Electronics stores), sporting_goods (Sporting goods stores), home_improvement (Home improvement), furniture (Furniture stores), online_retail (Online retail), office_supply (Office supply stores), shipping (Shipping and couriers), online_advertising (Social media and search advertising), other (Everything else).

merchant.description: Merchant name or web address as the user would say it or see it, e.g. "Whole Foods" or "delta.com", or a kind of place, e.g. "restaurants" or "gas station".

valuation.description: Instead of the user's saved point values (or earnrate's defaults): flat, points at their cash-out value, MR and UR at 1¢; or points-heavy, MR and UR at 1.7¢, for people who transfer points to airlines and hotels.

name: simulate_spending
title: Simulate a year of spending
